title: Learning to Decode Concatenated Quantum Codes with Hierarchical Message Passing
abstract: We introduce a neural message-passing framework for decoding general concatenated stabilizer codes. Soft beliefs propagate bidirectionally across concatenation levels, and lightweight neural networks learn only to aggregate incoming messages. For the concatenated $[[15,7,3]]$ quantum Hamming code, the resulting decoder achieves substantially higher thresholds than the state-of-the-art bidirectional hard-decision decoder under both bit-flip and depolarizing noise. In particular, the depolarizing pseudo-threshold nearly doubles, from $6.5\%$ to $12.3\%$. For many-hypercube codes, a decoder fine-tuned on circuit-level errors in Knill's teleportation-based error correction can achieve lower logical-CNOT failure rates than their dedicated decoder, using a fixed number of message-passing iterations instead of extensive combinatorial search. Our framework provides a generic decoding tool for exploring the design space of concatenated codes, including non-CSS constructions, toward low-overhead fault tolerance.

bite.hook: A new neural decoder nearly doubles the depolarizing pseudo-threshold for quantum codes from 6.5% to 12.3%.
tldr: Introduced a neural message-passing framework to decode general concatenated stabilizer codes.
Used bidirectional soft-belief propagation and lightweight neural networks that only learn to aggregate messages.
Achieved substantially higher thresholds and lower logical-CNOT failure rates under various noise models.
bite.whyItMatters: Building fault-tolerant quantum computers requires fixing errors efficiently without adding massive hardware overhead. This neural decoding framework makes complex quantum codes much easier to run accurately.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to fix a giant jigsaw puzzle where pieces keep flipping randomly. Instead of manually checking every piece, the researchers built a smart helper network that passes notes back and forth between puzzle sections to figure out the original picture much faster.

glossary.eli5Def: A smart way to protect fragile quantum information by constantly checking if anything changed without actually looking at the data.

glossary.eli5Def: Static or interference that randomly scrambles quantum information, making it forget what state it was in.
